observations.text: SP applied the emergency procedures to the standard desired for the Training Section, with the IP directing the simulated lost wingman sequence and completing part of the R/T relay to the ground station. Recall of the assistance duties toward the formation member suffering the emergency was demonstrated in the pre-flight briefing but was not converted into timely action in flight. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent initiation of the lost wingman procedure is expected to improve in the following sorties.

SP, after the IP's verbal prompts, completed the simulated lost wingman procedure from the Wingman position and informed the Leader of the loss of visual contact, with the omissions recognized and corrected with delay. The transition to IFR flight was performed safely and the ground station was contacted when the emergency A/C's R/T contact was simulated lost. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP informed the Leader in a timely manner of the loss of visual contact and initiated the predetermined lost wingman procedure without IP's intervention. Minor errors in the sequence of the emergency checklist items were recognized and self-corrected in a timely manner, and assistance to the affected formation member was provided as briefed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the emergency procedures accurately and rapidly throughout the mission, performing the lost wingman procedure as briefed and providing assistance to the formation member who suffered the simulated emergency. Ground stations were contacted without delay when the emergency A/C's R/T contact was simulated lost, and the transition to IFR flight from the Wingman position was safe and standardized. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy in the application of the formation emergency procedures, performing the predetermined lost wingman procedure without any prompting and providing immediate assistance to the formation member who suffered the simulated emergency. The R/T relay to the ground station and the analysis of the emergency in the post-flight briefing were above the levels desired for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an unrehearsed lost wingman flow, did not initiate the predetermined turn away from the last known position of the Leader and did not inform the Leader of the loss of visual contact. The IP had to direct the sequence and execute part of the R/T with the ground station. Further study of the formation emergency procedures is required.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorized recovery sequence, did not apply the emergency checklist for the simulated malfunction and did not provide the briefed assistance to the formation member suffering the emergency. The IP directed the procedure and completed the transition to IFR flight from the Wingman position. Recognition of the abnormal indication and initiation of the corresponding procedure did not occur without assistance.

SP applied the formation emergency procedures within the standards desired for the Training Section, completing the lost wingman procedure after the IP's verbal prompts. The call to the Leader and the request for the IFR clearance were made late, and the omissions were recognized and corrected only after prompting. Marginal performance for the Training Section - reduced reliance on prompting during the emergency sequence is expected to improve.

SP informed the Leader in a timely manner of the loss of visual contact and executed the predetermined lost wingman procedure without IP's intervention. Minor errors in the order of the emergency checklist items were recognized and self-corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the emergency procedures accurately and rapidly from engine start up to engine shut down, executing the lost wingman procedure as briefed and providing assistance to the formation member who suffered the simulated emergency. Contact with the ground station was established without delay when the emergency A/C's R/T was simulated lost. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy in the formation emergency procedures, performing the lost wingman procedure safely both as Leader and as Wingman and obtaining the IFR clearance without any prompting. Knowledge of the procedures was equally complete in the pre-flight and in the post-flight briefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized emergency checklist flow, did not complete the critical action items for the simulated malfunction and did not inform the Leader of the A/C state. The IP had to direct the procedure and execute part of the R/T relay to the ground station. Further study of the emergency procedures of the Contact and Formation Categories is required.

SP, due to absent explicit role assignment when the malfunction occurred, did not establish who was flying and who was working the procedure and did not provide the required assistance to the formation member suffering the emergency. The IP intervened, allocated the roles and completed the ground station contact on behalf of the emergency A/C. The procedure was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to an incomplete review of the lost wingman procedure in the pre-flight briefing, did not initiate the predetermined VMC lost wingman action at the loss of visual contact and did not inform the Leader in a timely manner. The procedure was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the error recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognized unsafe condition, did not declare the simulated emergency to the Leader and did not request the IFR clearance from ATC at the appropriate time. The transition to IFR flight from the Wingman position was performed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the omission was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP applied the formation emergency procedures within the desired standards, performing the lost wingman procedure and providing assistance to the affected formation member without IP's intervention. However, two items of the emergency checklist were completed out of sequence and the call to the ground station was made later than briefed, both self-corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in the sequence of the emergency actions is expected to improve.

SP applied the emergency procedures accurately and rapidly, executing the lost wingman procedure as briefed and providing immediate assistance to the formation member who suffered the simulated emergency. The Leader was informed in a timely manner, the transition to IFR flight was safe and the IFR clearance was obtained without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy in the application of the formation emergency procedures, performing the lost wingman procedure safely both as Leader and as Wingman in the simulated IMC segment. Assistance to the affected formation member and the R/T relay to the ground station were executed above the levels desired, with complete knowledge demonstrated in both briefings. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the lost wingman procedure applicable to the Wingman position, did not perform the predetermined turn and did not transition to IFR flight after the loss of visual contact in the simulated IMC segment. The IP had to direct the sequence and execute part of the procedure. Further study of the formation emergency procedures is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to locking onto one malfunction instead of continuing to fly the aircraft, did not complete the emergency checklist for the simulated failure and did not maintain the assistance duties toward the affected formation member. The IP intervened, took the A/C and completed the ground station contact for the emergency A/C. The procedure was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to a non-standardized emergency checklist flow, did not perform the critical action items in the prescribed order and did not inform the Leader of the simulated malfunction at the time briefed. The sequence was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the omissions recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a technically worded transmission where plain language was required to convey the emergency, did not state the condition of the emergency A/C to the ground station and did not obtain the IFR clearance at the first request. The transmission was reformulated only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the deficiency was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to an abbreviated review of the emergency checklist amplification, completed two items of the simulated emergency procedure out of the prescribed sequence while providing assistance to the affected formation member. The errors were minor, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased, delayed the call to the ground station on behalf of the emergency A/C whose R/T contact had been simulated lost. The lost wingman procedure and the transition to IFR flight were otherwise performed as briefed, and the delay was recognized and self-corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP applied the formation emergency procedures accurately and rapidly within the standards desired for the Training Section, performing the lost wingman procedure as Wingman and providing assistance to the formation member who suffered the simulated emergency. On one occasion the call to ATC for the IFR clearance was made at the late limit of the briefed timing, without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness of the ATC coordination during the emergency sequence is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy in the application of the formation emergency procedures throughout the mission, from engine start up to engine shut down, performing the lost wingman procedure safely both as Leader and as Wingman. Assistance to the affected formation member, the R/T relay to the ground station and the timely ATC coordination for the IFR clearance were executed above the levels desired for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
